questions.learningObjective: Identify the infinitive behind a conjugated form
questions.stem: Which infinitive does the form "tornavate" come from?
questions.explanation: The form "tornavate" is the imperfect form for "voi" of "tornare". Identifying the infinitive behind a conjugated form requires matching the stem and the person endings to the correct conjugation pattern.
questions.hint: Strip the ending and match the remaining stem to an infinitive.

questions.subject: ITALIAN
questions.stem: While annotating the text, a pupil studies one item for the check. Choose the subjunctive: "loro uscire".

options.misconception: this is the noi form of the verb, not loro
this is the io form of the verb, not loro
this is the voi form of the verb, not loro

questions.explanation: The subjunctive form of "uscire" for "loro" is "escano". The present subjunctive is used after expressions of doubt, wish, or necessity. It draws its stem from the third-person plural present. Selecting the wrong person ending changes who performs the action.
questions.hint: Identify the subject pronoun, then apply the subjunctive ending for that person.
